{{Short description|German chemist (born 1969)}}
[[File:PKraft.jpg|thumb|upright|Philip Kraft smelling on a [[gas chromatograph]] ]]
'''Philip Kraft''' (born in [[Rendsburg]] on March 24, 1969) is a [[Germans|German]] [[organic chemistry|organic chemist]]. Since 1996 he has been employed by [[Givaudan]], a leading Flavor and Fragrance company, where he designs [[captive odorant]]s for use in [[perfume]]s. He has lectured at the [[University of Bern]], the [[University of Zurich]], and the [[ETH Zurich]].

== Career ==
Kraft's interest in fragrance chemistry and perfumery was awakened in 1986 by an article on [[rose oxide]] analogs,<ref>Hoepfner, Wolfgang; Weyerstahl, Peter (1986). ''Liebigs Ann. Chem.'' '''1986''', 99–113.</ref> which led to contacts with Haarmann & Reimer (now [[Symrise]]), where he was introduced to the world of scents and fragrances. After graduation from high school and [[military service]] which involved [[forensic]] and [[analytical chemistry]], he studied chemistry from 1989–1994 at the [[University of Kiel]]. He obtained his degree while working in [[Werner Tochtermann]]'s group, then continued his research with this group, producing his [[PhD thesis]] on the [[Organic synthesis|synthesis]] of [[macrocyclic]] [[musk]]s in 1996. Moving to industry, he joined [[Givaudan]]'s Fragrance Research center of  in [[Dübendorf]] ([[Switzerland]]) in 1996 as the head of an organic synthesis laboratory. In 2001 he participated in an [[Exploration|expedition]] with [[Roman Kaiser]] to the primary [[rain forest]] of the [[Masoala]] [[peninsula]] ([[Madagascar]]) in search of new natural [[lead compounds|leads]]. That same year, he was promoted to group leader for the discovery of new odorants. His primary [[research]] interests are the rational design of new odorants, molecular modeling, and structure–odor correlations, particularly in the domain of [[musk]]s and floral odorants.<ref>{{cite journal | doi =10.1055/s-2005-918404 | last1 =Kraft | first1 =Philip | last2 =Popaj | first2 =Kasim | last3 = Abate | first3 =Agnese | journal =Synthesis | year =2005 | volume =2005 | pages =2798–2809 | title =Design, Synthesis and Olfactory Properties of 2-Substituted 2-tert-Butyl-5-methyl-2,5-dihydrofurans: seco-Derivatives of Theaspiranes | issue =16}} (Biographical sketch, English)</ref> Since 2008 he has taught courses in fragrance chemistry at the [[University of Bern]], the [[University of Zurich]], and the [[ETH Zurich]].

== Publications and patents ==
Kraft, as of 2014, has authored 78 papers in peer-reviewed chemistry journals, and is inventor or co-inventor of 30 patents. Highly cited reviews include “Fragrance Chemistry“,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Fráter | first1 = Georg | last2 = Bajgrowicz | first2 = Jerzy A. | last3 = Kraft | first3 = Philip | year = 1998 | title = Fragrance Chemistry". "Title | journal = Tetrahedron | volume = 54 | pages = 7633–7703 | doi=10.1016/s0040-4020(98)00199-9}}</ref> “Odds and Trends: Recent Developments in the Chemistry of Odorants”,<ref>{{cite journal | doi =10.1002/1521-3773(20000901)39:17<2980::AID-ANIE2980>3.0.CO;2-# | title =Odds and Trends: Recent Developments in the Chemistry of Odorants | year =2000 | last1 =Kraft | first1 =Philip | last2 =Bajgrowicz | first2 =Jerzy A. | last3 =Denis | first3 =Caroline| last4 =Fráter| first4 =Georg|journal =Angewandte Chemie International Edition | volume =2000 | pages =2980–3010 | issue =17}}</ref> “New and Unusual Natural Products of Fascinating Flower Scents“,<ref>{{cite journal | doi =10.1002/1521-3781(200101)35:1<8::AID-CIUZ8>3.0.CO;2-F | title =Neue und ungewöhnliche Naturstoffe faszinierender Blütendüfte: Überraschende Dufterlebnisse | year =2001 | last1 =Kaiser | first1 =Roman | last2 =Kraft | first2 =Philip | journal =Chemie in unserer Zeit | volume =2001 | pages =8–23}}</ref> and a book chapter on “Musks”.<ref>Kraft, Philip (2004). In ''Chemistry and Technology of Flavours and Fragrances'', Ed. Rowe, David J.; Blackwell Publishing Ltd., Oxford, 2004, pp. 143–168, {{ISBN|1-4051-1450-9}}.</ref> He co-organized the ''Flavor & Fragrance'' conference series of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] and the Society of the Chemical Industry in Manchester 2004 and London 2007, and the [[Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker]] at [[Leipzig]] in 2013.

Kraft was the research instigator and lead author of ''From Rallet No1 to Chanel No5 versus Mademoiselle Chanel No1''<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kraft|first1=Philip|last2=Ledard|first2=Christine|last3=Goutell|first3=Philip|title=From Rallet No1 to Chanel No5 versus Mademoiselle Chanel No1|journal=Perfumer & Flavorist|date=2007|volume=37|issue=October|pages=36–48}}</ref> which explored the work of perfumer [[Ernest Beaux]] leading to the creation of [[Chanel No.5|Chanel's No.5]].

== Invented Materials ==
* '''Super Muguet''' (6-ethyl-3-methyloct-6-en-1-ol, 2001), non-sensitizing [[Lily of the valley|muguet]] alcohol: »''Marc Jacobs Men''« ([[Hubert de Givenchy|Givenchy]], 2003).<ref>{{cite journal | doi =10.1002/(SICI)1099-0690(199911)1999:11<2781::AID-EJOC2781>3.0.CO;2-C | title =Synthesis of a Constitutional Isomer of Nerol by Consecutive Ireland-Claisen and Cope Rearrangements | year =1999 | last1 =Kraft | first1 =Philip | last2 =Eichenberger | first2 =Walter | last3 =Fráter | first3 =Georg |journal =European Journal of Organic Chemistry | volume =1999 | pages =2781–2785 | issue =11}}</ref>
* '''Azurone''' (7-isopentyl-2''H''-benzo[''b''][1,4]dioxepin-3(4''H'')-one, 2004), potent marine odorant: »''Oscar Marina Spirit''« ([[Oscar de la Renta]], 2005), »''Sécrétions Magnifiques''« ([[Etat Libre d'Orange]], 2007).<ref>{{cite journal | doi =10.1002/ejoc.200300174 | title =Conception, Characterization and Correlation of New Marine Odorants| year =2003 | last1 =Kraft | first1 =Philip | last2 =Eichenberger | first2 =Walter | journal =European Journal of Organic Chemistry | volume =2003 | pages =3735–3743 | issue =19}}</ref>
* '''[[Pomarose]]''' ((2''E'')-5,6,7-trimethylocta-2,5-dien-4-one, 2005), diffusive [[damascone]] mimic: »''Be Delicious for Men''« ([[DKNY]], 2005), »''Unforgivable''« ([[Sean John]], 2006), »''Unforgivable Woman''« ([[Sean John]], 2007), »''John Galliano''« ([[John Galliano]], 2008), »''1 Million''« ([[Paco Rabanne]], 2008), »''CK free''« ([[Calvin Klein]], 2009).<ref>{{cite journal | doi =10.1002/1099-0690(200106)2001:12<2363::AID-EJOC2363>3.0.CO;2-E | title =5,6,7-Trimethylocta-2,5-dien-4-one − A Suspected Odorant with Surprising Olfactory Properties | year =2001 | last1 =Kraft | first1 =Philip | last2 =Denis | first2 =Caroline | last3 =Eichenberger | first3 =Walter | journal =European Journal of Organic Chemistry | volume =2001 | pages =2363–2369 | issue =12}}</ref>
* '''Serenolide''' (2-(1-(3,3-dimethylcyclohexyl)ethoxy)-2-methylpropyl cyclopropanecarboxylate, 2006), linear musk odorant: »''Polo Double Black''« ([[Ralph Lauren]], 2006), »''Unforgivable Woman''« ([[Sean John]], 2007), »''John Galliano''« ([[John Galliano]], 2008).<ref>{{cite journal | doi =10.1002/ejoc.200800644 | title =New Musk Odorants: (3''E'')-4-(2-Alkyl-5,5-dimethylcyclopent-1-enyl)but-3-en-2-ones and (3''E'')-1-Acetyl-3-alkylidene-4,4-dimethylcyclohexenes| year =2008 | last1 =Kraft | first1 =Philip | last2 =Popaj | first2 =Kasim | journal =European Journal of Organic Chemistry | volume =2008 | pages =4806–4814 | issue =28}}</ref> This substance showed only weak potential for skin sensitization.<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1093/toxsci/kfm259 | title = Skin Sensitizers Induce Antioxidant Response Element Dependent Genes: Application to the in Vitro Testing of the Sensitization Potential of Chemicals | year = 2007 | last1 = Natsch | first1 = Andreas | last2 = Emter | first2 = Roger | journal = [[Toxicological Sciences]] | volume = 102 | pages = 110–9 | pmid = 17932397 | issue = 1| doi-access = free }}</ref>
* '''Sylkolide''' ((3' ''E'')-2-((3',5'-dimethylhex-3'-en-2'-yl)oxy)-2-methylpropyl cyclopropanecarboxylate, 2010), linear top-note musk: »''Core for Men''« ([[Gap (clothing retailer)|GAP]], 2010).<ref>{{cite journal | doi =10.1002/ejoc.200300578 | title =Synthesis and Odor of Aliphatic Musks: Discovery of a New Class of Odorants| year =2004 | last1 =Kraft | first1 =Philip | last2 =Eichenberger | first2 =Walter | journal =European Journal of Organic Chemistry | volume =2004 | pages =354–365 | issue =2}}</ref>
* '''Cassyrane''' (2-(''tert''-butyl)-5-methyl-2-propyl-2,5-dihydrofuran, 2010), sulfur-free cassis top note.<ref>{{cite journal | doi =10.1002/anie.201100937 | title =Cassis Odor through Microwave Eyes: Olfactory Properties and Gas-Phase Structures of all the Cassyrane Stereoisomers and its Dihydro Derivatives| year =2011 | last1 =Mouhib | first1 =Halima | last2 =Stahl | first2 =Wolfgang | last3 =Lüthy | first3 =Monique | last4 =Büchel | first4 =Michelle | last5 =Kraft | first5 =Philip | journal =Angewandte Chemie International Edition | volume =50 | pages =5576–5580 | issue =24 | pmid=21557421}}</ref>
